replies.author: LocoMod
replies.body:
Gamedev is the most difficult domain in programming because it basically spans all aspects of computer science and media. So you want the most intelligent models because programming is just one of many skills you need to have to make a game.

It is also well established that right now the absolute best coding model is Claude Opus 5.5 followed by GPT Astra. This may change in a few days/weeks, but today this is the best. Gemini 4 Carbon isn't widely available yet so few people have used it despite it being #1 in AA benchmark.

Programming a game can be done by most of the modern models. Making an actual good game is not guaranteed by any model. Most of the projects shown in this sub are not going to get finished even if they are being released in early access.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Hell no. Yes, chinese models like Kimi K3 are (much) cheaper but that is just one part of the story. In reality i get so much more out of Claude Ultra (formerly known as Claude  Max 20x) because i dont need a damn NASA computer at home to run the very best models on the market and on top of that Claude models are actually (easily) beating those chinese models in production where long term work matters and not a benchmaxxed 1 prompt showcase. Cheaper is not better and cheaper often means in reality more expensive mid to long term and other caveats of using cheap or cheaper solutions because of how cheaping out affects production. Been there with creative software, not (very) different with AI solutions.

You get what you pay for. In this case i pay more on the paper but i also get (much) more out of that which turns an investment into profit.
